title: A spiritual bouquet (II.7)
hookLine: after prayer, pick one thought like a flower to carry all day
tomorrow: before the phone, before coffee: what's the first move?

lines: HOW DO YOU TAKE A PRAYER WITH YOU?
A FEW FLOWERS FOR THE DAY.
cards: Leaving a wedding with a flower from the centerpiece. Walking out of a garden with a sprig of mint in your pocket. How do you take a prayer with you when you leave?
Francis de Sales borrows exactly that habit. People who've walked in a lovely garden, he says, don't like to leave without a few flowers to smell through the day.

teach.b: So he ends a meditation in two moves. First the conclusion: thank God for the good thoughts and resolutions you were given, offer them back, and ask for help to live them. Then the picking.
Choose one, two or three points that touched you most, and keep them close.
Through the day you come back to them and, in his phrase, smell them spiritually. Do the gathering right where you prayed, or walking alone a little while after.
The hour stays an hour; the bouquet is how it reaches the rest of the day.
And look what this week has already handed you. Philothea, the soul that loves God, living out in the world. The bee, honey without harm.
A faithful friend for the road. Clearing the ground, big stones first. Why made, from goodness and not need.
An hour, if you can. That's a bouquet already.
The old English word for a small bunch of flowers you hold close is nosegay. Pick one.

how: Some Catholics end their prayer by choosing a short thought or verse to return to through the day; in another custom, a 'spiritual bouquet' is a card promising prayers offered for someone.

o: a few thoughts from prayer carried through the day
flowers placed on the altar for a feast day
a list of prayers promised for someone's birthday

p: come back to them all day
a small bunch of flowers held close

s: de Sales's spiritual bouquet means real flowers left at a shrine
it's a few thoughts from prayer, carried and returned to through the day.
he says to gather the bouquet where you prayed, or walking alone after
the picking happens at the end of prayer, before the day takes over.
the bouquet replaces the hour of prayer
the hour stays an hour; the bouquet is how it reaches the rest of the day.

games.q: you finished a retreat with a notebook full of insights. by lunch on monday, it's all gone. what would de Sales have done before leaving?
o: picked one, two or three points and come back to them all day.
copied the whole notebook into his phone to reread later.
decided not to think about it until the next retreat.
games.why: a few flowers, not the whole garden. pick the points that touched you most and smell them through the day.

practice: Find something with a scent near you: a flower, coffee, a bar of soap, an orange peel. Breathe it in slowly while you choose one line from this week to go with it. Each breath in, the scent; each breath out, the line.

wordCard.voice: A spiritual bouquet. One, two or three thoughts gathered at the end of prayer, kept close and returned to all day.

carryVoice: Your line: a nosegay. A few flowers from prayer, small enough to carry in a pocket. That's the week.
